entities.summary: Clemens Andreas Denhardt (1852–1928) and his brother Gustav Denhardt (1856–1917), born in Zeitz, Province of Saxony, were distinguished German explorers of Africa at the time of the Scramble for Africa. In association with the physician G. A. Fischer they undertook in 1878 a tour through the Tana River region, East Africa, which they endeavored to secure to German commerce. Six years later they entered upon a second expedition, extending from the island Lamu to Vitu, where the Sultan of the Swahili requested the establishment of a friendly treaty with Germany based upon proposals made by him 18 years previously.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Clemens Denhardt's expeditions to East Africa in the late 19th century helped secure German commerce interests in the region, contributing to the Scramble for Africa. His efforts led to the establishment of a friendly treaty with the Sultan of Vitu.
